summary: Tested Items `usage` (sales/purchases/both) feature end-to-end. Backend: 10/10 pytest cases pass — default 'sales', explicit purchases/both, GET filter semantics (sales includes 'both', purchases includes 'both'), PATCH 400 on invalid usage, PATCH flip sales→purchases moves item across filters, legacy backfill returns non-null usage for every item, CSV import honours explicit 'usage' column and infers from expense-only account when column absent. Frontend: filter tabs (items-filter-all/sales/purchases/both) present with live counts, modal item-usage-picker with all 3 segmented buttons works, row badges use data-testid item-usage-{id}. Confirmed via network capture that Invoices page calls /items?usage=sales and Bills page calls /items?usage=purchases for the target company.

issues: Row badge uses data-testid=item-usage-{id} and modal picker buttons use data-testid=item-usage-sales/purchases/both — an item whose id equals literal 'sales'/'purchases'/'both' (extremely unlikely with UUIDs) would collide. No action required, but worth noting.

critical_code_review_comments: items.py list_items backfills `usage` on read but never persists it — every list call recomputes for legacy docs. Fine for correctness; consider a one-time backfill migration to reduce per-request work if item volume grows.

CSV import: usage inference relies on _infer_usage(inc_id, exp_id) which is called AFTER _resolve_account_for_type. When create_missing_accounts is False and no account matches, inc_id/exp_id are None so inferred usage silently falls back to 'sales' even if the CSV filled an expense column that failed to resolve — worth logging.
seed_data_creation: Test items prefixed with TEST_item_* / TEST_csv_* auto-created and cleaned up by pytest module fixture.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Items usage filter fully verified. If retesting, note that the frontend company switcher persists via server-side active-company (not simple localStorage) — use the top-bar company switcher UI to switch to Skyward Sparks if you want to see items in the /items page. XHR-level assertions (which is what matters for this feature) confirm invoices call ?usage=sales and bills call ?usage=purchases with the correct CID regardless.
